name: Tonsawang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hayes, Rebekah 2019, A morphosyntactic description of verbal constructions in Tonsawang (Univ. of London thesis); Sneddon 1978 Proto-Minahasan (read: no stress statement)

sources.citation: Brickell, Timothy C. 2018. Reduplication in Tondano and Tonsawang. NUSA: Linguistic studies of languages in and around Indonesia 65: 81-107.
sources.note: Sec. 3 phonological overview (inventories, phonotactics, syllable sequences, clusters for TDN and TNW); the words stress/accent do not occur; 'penultimate' only in coda-distribution statements.

sources.citation: Utsumi, Atsuko. 2018. Accent: Formosan and West Malayo-Polynesian languages (Austronesian). In: Studies in Asian Geolinguistics VIII, pp. 17-18. Tokyo: ILCAA, TUFS.
sources.note: Two-page survey + maps; text mentions for North Sulawesi only 'Talaud has stress on penult whereas stress is phonemic in Bantik and Ratahan'; Tonsawang/Minahasan not named in the text (map symbols not machine-readable).

sources.citation: Adriani, N. 1925. Uit en over de Minahasa III: De Minahasische talen. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 81: 134-164 (read in archive.org scanned text of the 1925 BKI volume, item dli.ministry.10294).
sources.note: Overview of the five Minahasan languages and their literature; no klemtoon/accent/nadruk statement found in the article span.

sources.citation: Utsumi, Atsuko (内海敦子). 2023. トンサワン語の文法概略: 形態音韻論と名詞句を中心に [A Brief Description of Tonsawang Grammar: Morpho-phonemics and Noun Markers]. 明星大学研究紀要 人文学部・日本文化学科 (Bulletin of Meisei University, Dept. of Japanese and Comparative Culture) 31: 170(25)-158(37).
sources.note: Sec. 2 'トンサワン語の音韻論' gives 6 vowels /i e a o u ə/, 18 consonants, cluster types, syllable template (CC)V(C), and 'softening' alternations; no statement on accent (アクセント) or stress (強勢) anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: Brickell, Timothy C. 2020. Language contact in North Sulawesi: Preliminary observations. NUSA 68: 159-190.
sources.note: Nothing on Tonsawang stress (only 'intonation' hit is a Manado Malay reference title).

sources.citation: Brickell, Timothy C. 2019 [2018]. Tonsawang (Toundanow), North Sulawesi, Indonesia - Language Contexts. Language Documentation and Description 16: 55-85. London: EL Publishing.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/vitality profile; no phonology. Notes (p. 78) that Kalangi (2012) Tonsawang-Indonesian dictionary 'also includes a small amount of information on phonology and morphology'.

sources.citation: Sneddon, J.N. 1978. Proto-Minahasan: phonology, morphology and wordlist. Pacific Linguistics B-54. Canberra: ANU. x+204 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3.1 'Tonsawang Phonology' (pp. 54-57) covers segmental phonemes, distribution and morphophonemics only; nothing on stress/accent for Tonsawang. The only stress mention in the book is note 90 (p. 192) on Tondano optional vowel lengthening 'when the word is stressed'.

sources.citation: van den Berg, René & David Mead. 2024. Languages of Sulawesi. In K.A. Adelaar & A. Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, 507-546. Oxford: OUP.
